_readme: The image lane's refusal rules, in ONE file because two languages enforce them:
src/core/imageCandidate.ts (apply-acquired, when a candidate is recorded) and
scraper/images.py (the fetch lane, when the bytes arrive). Two copies would drift the day one
of them changed and nothing would notice - the pipeline would keep fetching what the other
half already calls a placeholder (D:/Project/CLAUDE.md section 10, drifting copies).
placeholder_url_substrings are SUBSTRINGS of the lower-cased host+path, deliberately not
regexes: '\b' is the wrong tool for URLs and product strings alike (CLAUDE.md), and a
substring means exactly the same thing in JavaScript and in Python. Each one is here because
a real page served it as a 'product photo' - HPE's a50007032enw_complogoimg is the company
logo, printed in the same block as the product shot, and meraki's clipboard_ea330bc2....png is
somebody's pasted screenshot serving as an MG51's only picture. Check a new entry against the
corpus before adding it: 'catalog' does not contain 'logo', but something else might.
Two refusals are NOT here because a substring cannot express them, and both came out of the
first dry run over the real corpus (4 Sep 2026):
role != primary        five of ten leased candidates were ANTENNA RADIATION DIAGRAMS -
5ghz_wireless.png, Coverage-Patterns-6Ghz.png - real PNGs, well over
300 px, on white. The page called them 'gallery' and called the
product shot 'primary'. That is the only thing that separates them,
and it is enforced in the lease (scraper/images.py LEASE_SQL).
names-another-sku      meraki serves MR45.png as the MR46 page's primary image. A real photo
of a real product, just not this one. See other_sku_reason().
The names-another-sku rule refuses a SIBLING and accepts the part's OWN FAMILY, and the only
thing that separates the two is where the dash is (refined 4 Sep 2026, after run #50 refused
MS210-24P <- MS210.png: the family photo IS the product shot for every model in the family,
and the family slug is also a row in parts). The relation is read off the catalogue, not off
the string alone: a token only counts at all once it has been found to be a real parts.sku for
this vendor, and it is this part's ANCESTOR only when our SKU extends it across a dash -
MS210    -> MS210-24P      ancestor, accept: the dash separates a family from the port and
C9200L   -> C9200L-24P-4G  PoE configurations of ONE chassis.
MX64     -> MX64W          NOT an ancestor: a letter glued on with no dash is a DIFFERENT
MG41     -> MG41E          chassis - the W adds radios, the E moves the antennas outboard,
MX67     -> MX67C          the C adds an LTE modem. Different product, different photo.
MS250-48 -> MS250-48LP     the same shape, and refused for the same reason even though the
two switches look alike: PoE is a variant, not a configuration.
C9200    -> C9200L-24P-4G  a shared run of letters with no dash boundary is another family.
MR45 / MR46, MG41E / MG41  neither is a prefix of the other: siblings, always refused.
The catalogue's own shape corroborates the convention: MX64, MX67, MR45 and MR30H have ZERO
dash-children in parts, MS210 has 10, MS355 8 and C9200L 119. parts.family is NOT used and
must not be: it is a prose series label ('Cisco Meraki', 'UCS C-Series Rack Servers') that
never equals a PID, it is identical for MS210 and MS225-48FP, so equality on it would accept
ms210.jpg on the MS225-48FP page, and it is wrong outright on MR46 ('Catalyst 9800 Series
Wireless Controllers'). A file that names ANY sibling is refused even when it also names the
family: MS355-48X2-MS355-24X2-stacked.png names the MS355 family and two other models.
What a substring CANNOT express is counted instead, and those two rules do most of the work:
max_parts_per_url_key  one picture claimed by more parts than this is a category banner or
a family shot, not this part's photo. router-switch serves
'routers-cisco.jpg' on hundreds of unrelated product pages and no
pattern in the world recognises that filename as generic. Arista's
'banner/product/7050X3-product.png' is caught the same way, which is
why no '/banner/' substring is listed - it would also refuse the one
legitimate photo a single-product page carries.
max_parts_per_sha256   the same test after the download, on the BYTES: two URLs can serve
one placeholder. A vendor photo shared by a handful of SKUs in one
series is legitimate and stays under the limit.
min_long_side_px       below this a file is an icon, a swatch or a spacer, never a product
photo. It is far below Google Merchant's 800 px recommendation on
purpose: 'too small to be merchant-ready' is an ISSUE recorded
against the image, 'too small to be a photograph' is a REFUSAL.
merchant_min_long_side_px  Google Merchant's recommended minimum; below it the image is
still stored and still served, carrying ['below-800px'].
sku_family_separator   the one character that marks a family/configuration boundary in a
PID. Both halves read it from here rather than writing '-' twice.
sku_equivalent_suffixes  suffixes that name the SAME product, stripped before any SKU is
compared: '=' is Cisco's spare, '-HW' is Meraki's hardware-only SKU.
Both are REDUNDANT for other_sku_reason today - alnum() already drops
'=', and sku_tokens splits MR46-HW.png into MR46-HW AND MR46, so the
'names this part' branch carries it either way. They are here because
sku_relation() must be able to answer the question on its own; the
sabotage case is written at that level and says so, rather than
passing for a reason unrelated to the rule it names.
url_key_strip_segments are whole PATH SEGMENTS a CDN inserts for a rendition of the same
file; the filename (the last segment) is never dropped. After they are removed, adjacent
duplicate segments collapse, because a CDN that prefixes a rendition path repeats the segment
it prefixed: router-switch prints every photo twice, as
/media/catalog/product/cache/HASH/r/o/name.jpg  and
/media/mf_webp/jpg/media/catalog/product/cache/HASH/r/o/name.jpg
which are one picture and must cost one request, not two.
